issue.title: Gathering write support

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Use gathering writes if java version >= 7 and the ChannelBuffer is an instanceof CompositeChannelBuffer. See #267

This is mostly for discuss and testing

body:
I have bad news. I have tested the workaround this patch uses against a few linux distros and can confirm that it only appears to work for older distributions. It also will break MacOSX, since it requires the connect address to contain the % zone specifier.

I recommend reverting the workaround (or at least selectively enabling it for just Linux, and letting users know not all distros are covered).
Thats really bad.. I tested it with fedora 16. Maybe we should then allow to enable this workaround with a System Property . WDYT?

Ah it appears this was not the complete "hack". The problem with _just_ stripping the zone id is that it will prevent its purpose, which is to distinguish between multiple NICs that have the same link-local address. The full "hack" was to set the source binding address to use the non-stripped version, and the destination to use the stripped version. This hack fails on Fedora 16, 15, and updated 14, but it works on all versions of RHEL, and some versions of debian I had tested. Unfortunately the hack also breaks MacOSX/Darwin (you need the scope in the link local), and it probably breaks other platforms.

A system property is a good idea, although you might want to do the full hack. I'm not sure its worth it though. There might be other workarounds but it would take quite a bit of research, and you would have to selectively enable them per platform combination.
Isn't that what we do? We only use the stripped version for the remote address .

For the "hack" to work you have to strip AND you have to use the unstripped version as the bind address (another way to tell the OS which network interface to use when sending the packets), otherwise the OS will pick an ambigous interface or throw a routing error. Said another way, the whole reason to use a zoneid is to solve the ambiguity, so if you only strip it, you leave the ambiguity and defeat the purpose of it (intention of the user). They could just as easily not specify it if its not going to work anyway.

Yeah I know and that is what we do.. 

See for the bind:
https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/3/src/main/java/org/jboss/netty/channel/socket/nio/NioClientSocketPipelineSink.java#L126

And this for the connect:
https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/3/src/main/java/org/jboss/netty/channel/socket/nio/NioClientSocketPipelineSink.java#L141
Maybe I am missing something. I don't see anything in the above commits that calls bind with the zone id.

It calls bind with the given InetSocketAddress which will contain the zone id / scope id. The zone id / scope id will only get stripped of when it gets passed to the SocketUtil (which is only be used in the connect(..) method.
Ah ok reading the entire file I see that now. Any chance you were using openjdk on F16, that one seems to work with (and without) the workaround?
Ah now try the evil proprietary oracle sun jdk :)
I see... So I guess we should just make it configurable via System property or maybe remove the "workaround" all together and tell people to use java7 if they want to use ipv6 link-local addresses.
Yeah I think either approach is fine. I'll leave it to you to decide whats best. I only wanted to warn you that we were wrong about the workaround :(
I guess removing is the best. What will you do for jboss-as ? Will removing work for you ?

Yeah we are removing it everywhere we have it elsewhere and are just going to tell our users about the jdk bug, and the jdks we know that work. If I can find more time I'll try to research another workaround, but this could lead to a lot of variations so might not be worth it.
Ok I guess I will just remove it in netty too.. Thanks for all your efforts !
